title: Shantanu and Ganga

segments.voice: Yesterday: Devavrata, a river held back by arrows, and a father introduced to his own son.

Vasishtha. Ushanas. Brihaspati. Rama, the son of Jamadagni. That's the list Ganga gives the king. She's standing before Shantanu at the river's edge, holding their grown son by the hand, and before she lets go of him she tells his father what the boy has learned while he was away, and whose learning he holds. It's an extraordinary list. And the first name on it should make us stop.
screen: `A LIST OF TEACHERS.` → `SPOKEN AT THE RIVER'S EDGE.` → `THE FIRST NAME.`

segments.voice: He studied the Vedas, Ganga says, with Vasishtha. That's the sage whose cow was stolen, who cursed the Vasus, and who said the one who took her would live long on earth. The one who took her was Dyu. And Dyu is this young man. So the sage who sentenced him to a human life is the one who taught him how to live it. Then the list goes on. He knows everything Ushanas knows, the teacher the asuras follow, and everything Brihaspati knows, the teacher of the gods. And he knows every weapon known to Rama, the son of Jamadagni, the warrior sage tradition calls Parashurama. Take him home, she says. And she goes back into the water, and this time she doesn't return to the story for a long while. Shantanu brings his son to the capital and makes him heir to the throne, and the text says the people are glad of him. Step back, because this is the last day of Shantanu and Ganga, and the pieces fit. A king stared in heaven, and was born on earth to meet the river. Gods stole a cow, and were born to leave as fast as they came. A vow by a riverbank kept a father silent seven times. And the one who broke the vow saved the one son who was always meant to stay. One Vasu remains on earth, taught by the sage who cursed him, heir to a throne, and marked by that same curse to have no children. The next turn asks what that long life will cost him.
screen: `TAUGHT BY THE SAGE WHO CURSED HIM.` · `THE TEACHERS OF GODS AND ASURAS.` · `TAKE HIM HOME.` · `HEIR TO THE THRONE.` · then, large: `ONE VASU STAYS.`

segments.voice: Choose one ordinary thing your hands know how to do, cook a meal, drive, tie a knot, hold a child, and trace it back to whoever taught you, even someone you'd never have picked. Breathe in and feel the skill in your hands; breathe out and let a quiet thank you go to them, in whatever way is yours.
Gangeya. Ganga's son, taught by Vasishtha, Ushanas and Brihaspati, and given every weapon Parashurama knew, before his mother hands him back to his father as heir.
Your line: one Vasu stays. Next, a scent on the wind, and a woman with a boat. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Hindus set aside Guru Purnima, a full-moon day, to honor their teachers, and some students begin a course of study by touching the teacher's feet or offering a small gift.

notes: All paraphrase. Check Ganga's list in Ganguli: the Vedas with Vasishtha; all that Ushanas knows; all that Brihaspati knows; all the weapons of Rama, son of Jamadagni.
Ushanas (Shukra) as teacher of the asuras and Brihaspati as teacher of the gods are standard identifications given in the script's own words; confirm.
Rama son of Jamadagni is glossed as 'the warrior sage tradition calls Parashurama'; confirm.
'She doesn't return to the story for a long while' is a soft forward glance; confirm, or cut if a Keeper prefers.
Check that Shantanu installs Devavrata as heir apparent (yuvaraja) and that the text says the people were gladdened.
The link Dyu = Devavrata follows Ganga's explanation on day 707; Vasishtha teaching the Vasu he cursed is the script's observation from the text's details.
howItsDone mentions Guru Purnima and touching a teacher's feet as things some Hindus do; confirm the phrasing.

Editor (y3 audit): Ganga says he studied the Vedas with Vasishtha and knows what Ushanas, Brihaspati and Rama know, not that all of them taught him; the hook ('who taught him') and trapdoor now say so.
